To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a true random number generator based on sampling phase-jitter in oscillator rings can be made provably secure against a wide range of attacks, including active and fault attacks, by applying a resilient function to the analog output signal.
a random number generator with a high fill rate can be built with many fewer oscillators by using a resilient function, and that such a design is provably secure against fault attacks.

the fill rate is a good measure of the quality of a random number generator based on sampling phase noise in oscillator rings; that the fill rate decreases exponentially with the number of oscillations; that resilient functions are the right tool for extracting random samples from signals with low fill rate; and that the combination of these two techniques enables us to design provably secure random number generators with built-in tolerance to fault attacks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a provably secure true random number generator with built-in tolerance to active attacks.

the design proposed in this paper is provably secure and, therefore, it is suitable for applications where the highest level of security is needed.

our design is provably secure, in the sense that the probability of generating a bit with a given property (e.g., a given bit string or a given bit sequence) is bounded by the expected number of bits with that property.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a design that is provably random, provably secure, and with a provably high throughput.
we propose a provably secure design with a built-in tolerance to active attacks.
we have proposed and analyzed the first provably secure random bit generator based on oscillator phase jitter which is also tolerant to adversarial attacks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a provable security guarantee for a true random number generator is not a mere theoretical exercise but a practical design goal that can be achieved by a judicious choice of the underlying physical model, the postprocessing function, and the fault model.

the use of resilient functions in the design of true random number generator can provide provable resilience to a wide class of attacks, including active attacks, and that the use of such functions can also improve the performance of the system.
, in the context of true random number generation, the design of resilient functions is a fundamental tool to achieve a provably secure design.
